<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **50** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/frontend/layout.mdx`  _(via pageName (literal, a string literal in page))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/common-patterns.mdx`  _(via dashboardName (literal, a string literal in dashboard))_
- `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx`  _(via dashboardName (literal, a string literal in dashboard), pageName (literal, a string literal in page), reportName (literal, a string literal in report))_
- `content/docs/ui/reports.mdx`  _(via reportName (literal, a string literal in report))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via pageName (literal, a string literal in page))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via reportName (literal, a string literal in report))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (literal, 56 pages)`
- **29** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8749c7f16c2c0162a18014e8019ed8497ac74b00` — the merge of head `2c7d2600eb3e847383cf9e567fbdf89d81e23241` into base `bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8749c7f16c2c0162a18014e8019ed8497ac74b00 && git checkout 8749c7f16c2c0162a18014e8019ed8497ac74b00
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61 2c7d2600eb3e847383cf9e567fbdf89d81e23241 && git checkout -B drift-repro bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61 && git merge --no-ff 2c7d2600eb3e847383cf9e567fbdf89d81e23241

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**Verdict: ACCEPT at head `c0a6cf98d05340f4d3219d59d3e755d6abb3cd18`.** Landing waits for every check-run on that head to finish green.

1. **Shape.**
   - Draft PR → `main`. Line 1 is `Fixes #30290`, which is right: the whole card is delivered.
   - `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` sit at line start in both the body and the changeset.
2. **Premise and Clause-② measured.** The report states it measured the declaration closure of `dist/index.d.ts`, `console.d.ts` and `hook-body.d.ts` after a build: 39 files, 0 under `dist/lint`. The positive control (walking from `dist/lint/scenario-graph.d.ts`) finds 2. I read that as `no`. The seat did not rebuild.
3. **Diff and scope** (read via the PR files endpoint): 7 added files, +1306/−0. They are three modules plus three tests under `packages/cli/src/lint/`, and `.changeset/30290-scenario-scorer-port.md` (a patch for `@objectstack/cli`, which is a published package, so the changeset is owed). That is exactly the claimed surface.
   - Spot-checked the diff: provenance headers cite only issue numbers (`cloud#3600`, `cloud#2146`, `cloud#2149`) and carry no private cloud issue text.
   - No model or network call.
   - No CLI flag and no package-entry export.
4. **Gates.**
   - Dev side, each with its command and output: 3 files / 33 tests; the CLI unit tier 387 files / 5460 tests; typecheck; eslint. dispatch-gates: 59 derived, 57 run with exit 0, 2 NOT MEASURED with the prerequisite stated (they go to CI).
   - Check-runs on `c0a6cf98` at review time: 10 success, 13 skipped, the rest `in_progress`, 0 failure. Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are still running, so this is **not yet queue-eligible**.
5. **Accepted deviation.** The port is not byte-faithful: it closes two blind spots of the cloud source, which the discrimination self-test exposed.
   - Nav existence is now checked through app nav.
   - A widget bound to a missing dataset now fails its measure check.
   - Both are proven by ablation: with each check reverted, the degraded build scored 1 == intact 1.
   - This is the card's own acceptance ("degraded scores strictly lower"), so it is accepted.
6. **Out-of-scope findings and Skills-docs.**
   - The cloud source still carries both blind spots. Carrier: objectstack-ai/cloud#3604, which replaces `structural-score.ts` with an import of this module (pointer posted there).
   - `Skills-docs:` is not owed (`Metadata-protocol: none`).
   - Landing: once every check is green, the seat flips this PR to ready and enables auto-merge through the relay.

**Verdict: ACCEPT at head `2c7d2600eb3e847383cf9e567fbdf89d81e23241`.** This replaces the ACCEPT on `c0a6cf98`, which the head move spent. Landing waits for every check-run on this head to finish green.

It is inside the amended file surface (card comment 6651380112).
2. **Class checked.** The row is `not-a-served-read`, the same arm as the existing `packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts` precedent ("authoring-time static analysis of metadata; reads no record"). The reason matches the code: `artifactToEvalGraph` reads a declared reference target out of a built artifact, and no record is read or served.
3. **Reproduction.** The pin is red at `c0a6cf98` ("unclassified - packages/cli/src/lint/scenario-graph.ts", 1 failed / 3 passed) and green at `2c7d2600` (4/4). The 3 scorer suites stay 33/33. dispatch-gates re-derived 61 families; the 2 new ones exited 0.
4. **Check-runs on `2c7d2600` at review time:** 14 success, 8 skipped, 18 in_progress, 0 failure. Not yet queue-eligible.
5. **PR body note.** The body does not list the pin row. This record is where it is stated: `packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts` gains one `CALLERS` row classifying `scenario-graph.ts` as `not-a-served-read`.
6. **Landing.** Once every check is green, the seat flips this PR to ready and enables auto-merge through the relay. Items 2–6 of the round-0 record stand unchanged.
